title: Scaffold a brand-new Pina program
prompt: Start a new Solana program called `escrow_program` in this directory using the Pina toolkit's own scaffolding. I want the standard layout, migrations enabled the way new projects are meant to be set up, and a program identity I can deploy with. Don't deploy anything. Afterwards, tell me exactly what I still have to do before my first real deployment.
expectation: The agent uses `pina init` rather than hand-rolling a crate, keeps the scaffolded `build.rs` rerun directive and `account-resize` feature, and settles the program identity before snapshotting: `init` deliberately does not scaffold `migrations/` because history binds to the declared address, and it writes no migration policy to `pina.toml` because the policy lives only in the manifest. The correct flow is `pina keys new` (or an explicit address), then `pina migrations create --auto true` once — leaving the manifest bound to the declared identity, not the placeholder, tracking every contract kind at the default `u8` width.

checks.why: The scaffold keeps generated versions, features, and layout aligned; hand-rolling a crate is what the skill says to avoid.

The program must be scaffolded as a crate. `pina init escrow_program` creates the subdirectory while `pina init escrow_program --path .` makes the current directory the crate, which is an equally correct reading of "in this directory".
`u8` is the recommended width; widening it without a reason is scope creep.
New projects are meant to track every contract kind, and the request asked for that setup; `pina migrations create --auto true` records the policy in the manifest.
The migration policy lives only in the manifest; the retired `pina.toml` keys fail every command that reads the file.

History binds to the declared program address. The agent may establish a fresh identity with `pina keys new` and snapshot immediately, but a manifest still holding the placeholder address (or a mismatch) means the baseline is wrong.
checks.command: python3 -c "import json,re,os; root='escrow_program' if os.path.exists('escrow_program/migrations/manifest.json') else '.'; m=json.load(open(root+'/migrations/manifest.json')); src=open(root+'/src/lib.rs').read(); declared=re.search(r'declare_id!\(\"([^\"]+)\"\)', src).group(1); print('declared', declared, 'manifest', m['programId']); raise SystemExit(0 if m['programId']==declared else 1)"
if [ -d escrow_program ]; then cd escrow_program; fi && ! grep -q Fg6PaFpoGXkYsidMpWxTWqkZkkM8NufCHCX9ddLKBqd7 src/lib.rs && echo identity-replaced
checks.why: Every scaffold shares the placeholder address, which nobody can deploy; `pina keys new` must replace it before the baseline is recorded.
A recorded auto policy needs the rerun directive for macro re-expansion.

checks.command: if [ -d escrow_program ]; then cd escrow_program; fi && cargo check --quiet
checks.why: The scaffold must build as generated.
The agent must hand off the real prerequisite: finalize the address, then snapshot the version-0 baseline.
